The cost of packaging increased in April.
We missed the target by two million.
The bottom line did not move at all.
The margin fell two points, because the cost increased.
We did not reach the target, and I can tell you why.
The new line broke even in month five.
Sales looked great, and the bottom line did not move.

Good morning, everyone. I recorded this because I wanted the whole sales team to hear the same thing at the same time. The second quarter closed last Friday, and I will give you the numbers before anybody reads them somewhere else. Revenue grew eleven percent, and volume grew eight. Those are the two best numbers we have had in three years, and I want you to hear that first, because the rest of the message is harder. The margin fell two points. The cost of packaging increased fourteen percent in April, and nobody changed the price list after that, so we absorbed all of it. That is not a sales problem, and it is not a finance problem. It is a decision that nobody made. So here is what I need for Thursday. Bring me the three accounts where you gave the biggest discounts last quarter, and the reason for each one. Not a spreadsheet. Three names, three reasons. Thank you.

I read this report twice, and the second time I stopped looking at the line everybody looked at. The market saw revenue growth of eleven percent and decided the quarter was good. I went straight to the margin, because the margin is where a quarter tells you the truth. And the margin fell two points. Now, a falling margin is not automatically bad news. It is bad news when it happens by accident. What I see here is a company that bought its growth with discounts. It sold more units at a lower price instead of raising the price list when its own costs went up. That can be an excellent decision, if you are buying market share on purpose and you know exactly what you are paying for it. This report does not tell me that. So there is one thing, and only one, that I will watch in the third quarter: whether the margin comes back without losing the volume. If it does, this was a decision. If it does not, it was an accident, and the fourth quarter will be worse.
Revenue grew eleven percent last quarter.
The margin fell two points, because the cost increased.
We did not reach the target, and I can tell you why.
The new line broke even in month five.
Sales looked great, and the bottom line did not move.
The cost of packaging increased fourteen percent in April.
